_: Stakeholders a risk can be assigned to. reports_to is the escalation edge — a risk rises along it until a role accepts it. null = the top.

items.label: SRE / platform on-call
items.lens: keeping the service up, and being the one paged when it is not

items.label: Platform owner
items.lens: what runs in production and what it is allowed to touch

items.label: Customer-facing service owner
items.lens: what the customer experiences when this goes wrong

items.label: CISO
items.note: The line worth arguing about: every security risk escalates through the person accountable for delivery.
items.lens: whether the organisation can say what happened, and prove it

items.label: CTO
items.lens: whether the estate can be changed safely at the speed the business wants

items.label: Chief Product Officer
items.note: Owns what the product does to a customer, which is where an agent's output lands.
items.lens: what the product does to the people who use it

items.label: CFO
items.note: Owns the money shape of an exposure: cost of loss, cost of control, cost of stopping.
items.lens: what this costs, and what it costs if it goes wrong

items.label: DPO
items.note: Sits under the CFO here, which is the common corporate arrangement. GDPR Art. 38(3) requires the DPO to report to the highest management level — so this line is the one to argue about in a real estate, and moving it is a single field.
items.lens: whether a person's data is handled lawfully and can be accounted for

items.label: CEO
items.note: Appointed by the board, and reports to it. Every executive line converges here first.
items.lens: the whole of it, because everything arrives here eventually

items.label: Board
items.note: Everything arrives here. Acceptance below decides whether the board must ACT on it, never whether it sees it.
items.lens: whether the organisation is being run in a way they can defend
